title: Choose YAFFW's replacement visual world
question: The proof-desk world was assigned. Keep it, take a dealt alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Prepress Proof Desk
options.lineage: print-production imposition sheets, registration proofs, and delivery dockets
options.thesis: One media asset becomes a proof: inspect it, bracket the keep, then tear off the finished output.
options.viewport: A near-white proof field carries one oversized media frame, a single horizontal evidence strip, and a narrow delivery docket at the right edge.
options.risk: Print grammar can feel mannered if crop marks become decoration instead of structure.

options.label: Sixteen-Color Utility
options.lineage: Japanese PC-98 production software and locked sixteen-color fields
options.thesis: A fixed-region editing utility where every state is a decisive cell, never a floating card.
options.case: Strong product clarity and authored character; audience identification depends on accepting a deliberately retro computer grammar.
options.viewport: The media owns the upper-right field while one low text window and a fixed left command bank expose Selection and export state.
options.risk: Pixel nostalgia can overpower quick-task clarity when labels become codes.

options.label: Amber Darkroom
options.lineage: printing darkrooms, exposure test strips, and safelight work bays
options.thesis: The source image develops in stages while one test strip previews the Selection before export commits.
options.case: Immediate media-world identification, but the slow irreversible ritual conflicts with YAFFW's quick occasional use.
options.viewport: A full-width developing image dominates the field with one exposure strip below and sparse timer controls at the edge.
options.risk: The chemical sequence can imply more waiting and commitment than the product actually requires.

options.label: Live Specimen
options.lineage: interactive variable-type specimens and foundry proof sheets
options.thesis: One giant preview and one continuous axis make the selected range feel immediate and tactile.
options.case: Excellent at eliminating containers, but it identifies as typography software before it identifies as a media editor.
options.viewport: The loaded media behaves like a giant specimen above a single range axis and tiny monospaced output coordinates.
options.risk: Scale contrast may obscure secondary audio and export states.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark central viewer, inspector, transport bar, and stacked timeline executed with impeccable restraint.
canonCard.viewport: The conventional editor arrangement, simplified and polished around one active asset.
canonCard.risk: It resolves quickly but returns to the category language and nested panel structure the redesign is meant to escape.
